note_for_at_34_e3_004:
NOTE FOR AT-34-E3-004 AND THE BUNDLE RETROSPECTIVE

This file is a DERIVED, PARTIAL input. It does not satisfy AT-34-E3-004, whose bar is a
per-bucket measured cost recorded by the cycles themselves. It exists because 12 of 13
bucket-B cycle receipts recorded no wall time at all, and a cost reconstructed later from
memory is not a measurement. Deriving it from git while the commits were fresh is the
closest honest substitute.

Two caveats that bound how far it can be pushed:
  1. Wall time is a commit-to-commit span, so it includes queue and dispatch overhead and
     is an UPPER bound on any single cycle's real cost.
  2. units_closed is corpus-wide, not core_rulebook-only. A generic fix closes units in
     books nobody was working on, which is precisely the effect being measured -- but it
     means these figures must never be quoted against a single book's denominator.

What it establishes, and it is the load-bearing finding for scoping the remaining books:
cost is per CYCLE, not per unit. 2 generic corpus-wide cycles closed 2,003 units in 348
minutes (345 units/hour). 11 narrow book-scoped cycles closed 234 units in 703 minutes
(20 units/hour). The same engineering effort yields roughly 17x more when the cycle is
scoped to a mechanism corpus-wide rather than to one book's slice of it.
